solution.title: Migrating the Microsoft Entra Connect Source Anchor to mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid for AD Domain Consolidation & Cross-Forest Migration (Quest On Demand Migration)

products.name: Migrating the Microsoft Entra Connect Source Anchor to mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid for AD Domain Consolidation & Cross-Forest Migration (Quest On Demand Migration) — Commercial
products.short_description: Consolidating AD with Quest On Demand Migration while Entra Connect still uses objectGUID? Switch the source anchor to mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid the safe way — seamlessly for existing users, proven by a hard-match pilot — so the migration doesn't orphan your Entra identities. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Don't let the domain consolidation orphan your Entra identities

You're consolidating Active Directory — remapping accounts into a target domain or forest with Quest On Demand Migration — but your Microsoft Entra Connect Sync deployment still uses objectGUID as its source anchor. That older default is a landmine: objectGUID is regenerated when an object moves to a new domain or forest, so every migrated account looks like a brand-new identity to Entra. The result is duplicate or orphaned cloud accounts — users lose their mailbox, licenses, and Teams. This solution switches the source anchor to mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid safely, on a live deployment, without re-syncing users or creating duplicates, so Quest can carry the anchor across each move and Entra Connect hard-matches every migrated object to its existing cloud user.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run, read-only PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths and explicit Gates A–E; every object and artifact is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable identity-migration engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every consolidation.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with a decisive Quest hard-match test before any production wave.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — why objectGUID breaks on migration, why mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid survives (and how Quest ODM stamps it onto the target), what the wizard switch actually does, and why it's seamless for existing users.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (current Connect build, current anchor, the empty-attribute precondition, connector-account write permission, a configuration backup, the Quest stamp, AD FS ports if federated, roles, tenant) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — ordered steps in five phases with explicit gates: assess the anchor/version/precondition/permission and back up, switch the anchor in the Entra Connect wizard, pilot one Quest migration and confirm a hard-match, validate no duplicates and unchanged immutableId, then expand into the production waves.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — read-only assessment, precondition testing, connector-permission checking, post-change validation (anchor value unchanged), and coverage/duplicate-risk reporting. (The anchor change itself is done in the wizard, by design — never scripted.)
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for a safe, one-way anchor migration.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation with Gates A–E, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run, read-only scripts:
    • SRCANCHOR-Assess.ps1 — report the current source anchor, the Connect Sync version, and whether mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid is populated in-scope, with a readiness verdict
    • SRCANCHOR-Test-Preconditions.ps1 — list any in-scope objects that already have mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid set (the wizard blocker)
    • SRCANCHOR-Check-Permissions.ps1 — verify the AD DS connector (sync) account can write mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid on each in-scope OU (per-OU PASS/FAIL)
    • SRCANCHOR-Validate.ps1 — confirm the anchor is now mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid and its value equals the prior immutableId (seamless, no duplicates)
    • SRCANCHOR-Report.ps1 — coverage and duplicate-risk report across the in-scope population

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each consolidation feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

The source anchor migrated from objectGUID to mS-DS-ConsistencyGuid on a live deployment — seamlessly for existing users, with the connector permission and backup in place, proven by a Quest hard-match on a pilot before the production waves. The domain consolidation proceeds without orphaning a single Entra identity.

Delivered as a PDF implementation guide plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
